machines._doc: Locks shared with rsk-perf-lab in ~/.research-lab/locks (bin/lib.sh). A campaign holds this Mac's Docker slot as a long holder, so perf-lab's short replays and gates go first.

mainnet_seed._doc: perf-lab's mainnet seed (rsk-database-seed): the one thing read from another checkout, because the 186 GiB seed exists once. volume holds /seed (RSKj) and /rustock-seed; runs use hard-link clones in it. k6 is the rskj-k6-tests checkout live arms drive the node with (bin/live-arm.sh).

live._doc: Live mining arms (bin/live-arm.sh, docs/live-mining-plan.md): each client mines its own blocks under k6 for arm_minutes, in a container with these limits (perf-lab's live arms: 2 CPUs, 10 GB on the mainnet seed). The first min_block blocks of every arm are dropped (k6 deploys its contracts there); an arm counts only with min_qualifying_blocks blocks at least threshold full, a k6 success rate (k6_success_metric per k6 option, from the k6 summary) of at least k6_min_success_pct, and its blocks replayed into the other client with the same hashes. mining_coinbase is where rustock sends block rewards (RSKj derives its own from miner.coinbase.secret); REMASC pays either out 4000 blocks later, so neither arm sees the reward.

rskj._doc: RSKj in the harness. Measured at the head of perf-lab/integration (everything rsk-perf-lab has proven), recorded per campaign.
rskj.settings: conf/rskj/rsk.conf (rskip144 off, rskip97 at 0), conf/rskj/logback.xml, -Xms2G -Xmx4G, flushNumberOfBlocks 10

rustock._doc: rustock in the harness. Built from the harness adapter branch until its upstream pull requests merge. import_args: rskj's regtest chain as the lab's rsk.conf sets it (genesis file, rskip97=0, rskj's gas-limit bounds, skipPowValidation), the trie in its own RocksDB (a fresh data dir with the default single backend is refused by the fork), flush every {flush} blocks like RSKj.
rustock._mainnet_doc: mainnet_import_args: like import_args but on a hard-link clone of the converted mainnet seed ({datadir} = the clone, rustock's own layout as --import-rskj wrote it: one RocksDB with the trie inside, network id 30), with every --hardfork and --consensus-rule of rsk-perf-lab's database-seed/seeds/mainnet/node.props behind --allow-chain-overrides (harness/mainnet-overrides). tbd1000 is accepted as a no-op: it only turns on RSKIP-559, which rustock does not implement and no sample block exercises. No genesis: mainnet's is built in.
rustock._live_doc: live_args (bin/live-arm.sh): the replay flags without --import-blocks, serving RPC on 4444 for k6, with the ten cow keys from conf/rustock-wallet.keys ({wallet}, the fork's regtest-wallet.example.keys) so eth_sendTransaction signs for the accounts the genesis funds, the account rate limiter off as in RSKj's rsk.conf, the evm_* namespace for evm_startMining, timed mining at a 10 s median like RSKj's TimedMinerClient (--mine-timed, adapter harness/timed-mining) with nonce 0 under --skip-pow-validation, the trie flushed every {flush} mined blocks and the mined-block breakdown line (adapter harness/mined-block-timing) in {breakdown}. export_args (adapter harness/export-blocks) writes blocks {from}..{to} in RSKj's ExportBlocks format to {file} for the cross replay, on a stopped data dir. The adapter branches are being written: --mine-timed, --flush-every and the --export-* flags may land under other names, and live-arm.sh reads whatever is here. mainnet_* are the same on top of mainnet_import_args.
rustock._mainnet_args_doc: mainnet_*_args: the same regtest configuration as *_args on the converted mainnet seed, whose trie lives in the single RocksDB backend. The seed runs as regtest (chain id 33, conf/genesis_25M.json, every hardfork at genesis): that is how RSKj mines on it in perf-lab (--regtest plus node.props), so the sample's transactions carry chain id 33.
